process_lessons.TF1: A frozen configuration may legitimately yield zero candidates; zero yield does not justify weakening gates.
process_lessons.TF2: Full-dimensional convex hulls over many features can create enormous opaque facet families.
process_lessons.TF3: One-feature ratios improve readability but often encode bounded-order scale rather than stable structure.
process_lessons.TF4: Fixed pairwise hulls recover interpretable low-dimensional geometry without TF2-style opacity.
process_lessons.TF5: Finite survival plus an exact-form negative search can conceal stronger published fixed-parameter results.
process_lessons.TF6: Awkward scale does not justify deleting or normalizing an invariant with genuine structural recurrence.
process_lessons.TF7_TF8: Facet relations can expose real structural mathematics even when the original candidates do not graduate.
process_lessons.TF9: Independently derived mathematics can be subsumed by stronger prior art; significance and novelty are separate.
